newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Minor violence mars Indonesia election campaign.
newsitem.headline: Minor violence mars Indonesia election campaign.

text.p: Several people were injured in violence involving supporters of Indonesia's ruling Golkar party during election campaigning in the capital Jakarta on Thursday, witnesses said.
It was the latest in a series of minor clashes which have hit campaigning for the May 29 general elections.
Witnesses said Golkar supporters passing a construction site in a southern suburb of the capital demanded the workers there join them in shouting political slogans.

The workers refused and heavy stone-throwing erupted from both sides. Several people sustained head wounds, but the fighting died down before squads of armed troops and anti-riot police reached the scene, the witnesses said.

The windshields of more than 20 cars were damaged and stones littered the main thoroughfare adjoining the construction site. Witnesses said none of those injured appeared to be badly hurt although several were led away bleeding.
Police at the site refused to comment and there was no official word on the incident.
Earlier, police said there were sporadic clashes on Wednesday as supporters of the minority United Development Party (PPP) campaigned in Central Java province and Jakarta.
The reports of violence hit financial markets in the city, which were already nervous because of the spreading effects of steep falls in Thailand's currency and stock market.
The rupiah closed in Jakarta at the day's low of 2,442.00/43.00 against the dollar from a 2433.50 open while the local stock market index ended down 1.98 percent at 656.99 points.
The biggest clash on Wednesday came during campaigning by the Moslem-oriented PPP near Temanggung, 400 km (250 miles) southeast of Jakarta in Central Java.
Police and army sources in Temanggung and surrounding towns said thousands of PPP supporters turned violent in the province, which has seen repeated trouble in the past few weeks.
"It's quiet again today, but yesterday they attacked this police station and caused serious damage," a policeman at Kedu precinct, who did not give his name, told Reuters by telephone.
"There were no arrests and no serious injuries," he added.

The minority PPP and the Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) are battling the ruling Golkar for 425 seats in parliament. Another 75 seats in the house are allotted to the military, which does not vote.

The Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Thursday that PPP supporters attacked government offices, shops, churches, other buildings and cars while burning Golkar flags during a 10 km (six mile) march near Temanggung involving 6,000 people.

The newspaper said participants wore white, the traditional colour of mourning or protest, instead of the PPP's usual green, because of unfair treatment by authorities and the beating of their supporters by security forces.
In Jakarta a police station in Ciracas in the east of the capital was slightly damaged on Wednesday when a crowd of PPP supporters attacked it.

The official Antara news agency quoted Jakarta police spokesman Lieutenant-Colonel Edi Aritonang as saying the incident occured after a campaigner was detained for extorting money in a nearby market. Two policemen were slightly injured in the incident and three people were detained.
Residents said there were also clashes between PPP supporters and youths living in a military housing complex in south Jakarta who supported Golkar.

Golkar, in power for the last 30 years under President Suharto, is seeking to push its share of the vote to more than 70 percent from the 68 percent it won at the last polls in 1992. The PPP won 17 percent and the PDI 15 percent.
